exposure: labor and delivery unit capacity and staffing
outcome: association between hospital characteristics and intrapartum practices with cesarean rate
cohort: Nurse managers or other clinical staff knowledgeable about intrapartum care from 39 hospitals (out of 60 eligible) in Connecticut and Massachusetts
finding: Intrapartum practices varied markedly across hospitals, with some practices (e.g., offering cesarean on request, liberal indications for induction and cesarean) associated with higher cesarean rates, while others (e.g., having certified nurse-midwives, permitting eating during labor) were associated with lower rates.
